sources.note: Only a family-wide generalisation for all South-East TNG languages, p. 622: 'Some languages are tonal but stress is generally important and related to intonation which may be quite complex.' sources.note: Section 2.5 Stress, p. 605: 'The stress on a word is usually on the second last syllable. Although it does sometime occur on the third last syllable, it never occurs on the last syllable in a polysyllabic word' - but this is MAGI/Mailu (mail1250), a sister language, not Binahari.

sources.citation: Thomson, N.P. 1975b. The dialects of Magi. In T.E. Dutton (ed.), Studies in Languages of Central and South-East Papua, pp. 37-90. Pacific Linguistics C-29.
sources.note: Section 2.12.3 Binahari (pp. 47-48): Ma and Neme'a share only 60% basic vocabulary and are treated as two separate Mailuan languages under the blanket name Binahari; comparative wordlists only, no stress.
